subtitulo: Fui, comí, me encantó — three past-tense verbs that turn your trip into a story worth telling
cena: Someone genuinely wants to know what you did yesterday, and everything you know how to say is stuck in the present tense.
decisao: usar tres verbos no passado (fui, comí, me encantó) pra contar o dia de ontem, em vez de descrever tudo no presente
frasePiso: You don't need every past tense in the language. You need three verbs, and you already know all three.

steps.pt: Everything so far lived in the present — order this, ask that. Today: three verbs that turn yesterday into a story.
Fui — I went. The whole day starts with where you went, and that one word carries the whole sentence.

steps.promptPt: Say where you went yesterday. Speak now.

steps.pt: Comí — I ate. Same pattern, different verb. The story is building itself one short sentence at a time.

steps.promptPt: Say what you ate. Speak now.

steps.pt: The verb that closes with feeling: me encantó — literally 'it delighted me,' but it lands like 'I loved it.'

steps.promptPt: Say you loved it. Speak now.

steps.pt: And what are you going to do today?
The conversation swings forward too — no new tense needed, vamos a plus what you'll do covers tomorrow.

steps.promptPt: Say what you're going to do today. Speak now.
steps.es: Vamos a ir a la playa.
steps.pinyin: BAH-mohs ah eer ah lah PLAH-yah
steps.pt: We're going to go to the beach.
steps.tts: Vamos a ir a la playa.

steps.promptPt: They described the festival. Ask to see it. Speak now.
They described somewhere from years ago. Ask if it is still there. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can I still see that place?

steps.promptPt: Invite the longer story. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: meh PWEH-deh kohn-TAHR KOH-moh EH-rah AHN-tehs
steps.pt: Can you tell me what it was like before?

steps.promptPt: Swing the conversation forward. Speak now.
steps.pt: Do you have any recommendation for tomorrow?

steps.es: Fui al mercado. Comí tacos al pastor. Me encantó.
steps.pinyin: fwee al mehr-KAH-doh. koh-MEE TAH-kohs al pahs-TOR. meh en-kahn-TOH
steps.pt: Shadow the whole story: went, ate, loved it.
steps.tts: Fui al mercado. Comí tacos al pastor. Me encantó.

steps.pt: I06 complete. Fui, comí, me encantó make yesterday a story, vamos a covers tomorrow — past and future, not just present.

aprofundar.titulo: Three verbs is a whole trip

secoes.corpo: Fui, comí and me encantó are specific examples of a much larger past tense (the preterite), but you don't need the grammar rule to use these three correctly and often.

secoes.titulo: Me encantó is grammatically backwards, on purpose
secoes.corpo: Like gustar, encantar puts the thing doing the delighting first. Me encantó literally means 'it delighted me' — you don't need to unpack that to use it naturally.

secoes.titulo: Vamos a is the easiest future
secoes.corpo: Rather than learning a separate future tense, vamos a plus a plain verb ('we're going to...') does the job for almost anything you'd want to say about your plans.

permissao: You are allowed to tell your whole day with exactly three verbs. Fui, comí, me encantó is not a simplified version of the story — for a conversation with someone you just met, it's the complete story.
espelho: Telling a friend 'went to the market, had tacos, loved it' in English is already the natural, compressed way most people actually talk about their day — Spanish just asks you to carry that same compression in three specific verb forms instead of English's more flexible past tense.
